description: Works to trees covered by LBE ORDER NO 45 (1976): PROPOSAL A - (T12) Common hawthorn - remove north and northwest limbs at 3m, (T12) common hawthorn - remove hanging limb growing over the south at 4m, (T17) Acacia - re-pollard by up to 4m to previous points, (T21) Lime - remove dead limb at west,  (T28) Common ash - prune by up to 3m to clear structure/wires/buildings.PROPOSAL B - (T26) Acacia - remove west branch overhanging footpath
decision_conditions: This consent is valid for two years.Reason: In order that the nature of work pertaining to this consent remains appropriate.

The works hereby approved shall only be carried out strictly in accordance with British Standard 3998 [2010] 'Tree Works'. The works to T28 ash shall be strictly limited to that which is necessary for the creation of up to 3m clearance between the built structure and the remaining foliage only. Previous pruning points shall not be exceeded, meaning that in some places, 3m will not be achievable.Reason: In the interests of the health, safety and appearance of the preserved trees.

Tree work should not be carried out during periods that are likely to interfere with or disturb breeding birds or mammals.Reason: In order to comply with the requirements of the Wildlife and Countryside Act (1981) and Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations (2010).

No branch is present at 2.5m height from ground level, as described within the application documents. A split is present on the tensile (east) side of the stem. Branches originating from this area of the stem should be the subject of an application seeking to shorten them rather than remove them back to source, thus reducing the load on the defective part whilst still retaining branch structure and keeping pruning wounds away from already compromised parts.
